What is an ADU, and which type fits your lot?

An accessory dwelling unit, or ADU, is a smaller, self-contained home on the same lot as a main house. It has its own entrance, kitchen and bathroom. You may also hear it called a backyard cottage, granny flat, in-law suite or backyard tiny home.

The common types

  • Detached ADU. A separate building in the yard. It offers the most privacy and the most design freedom.
  • Attached ADU or addition. Joined to the main house, sometimes by a breezeway.
  • Garage conversion. Turns an existing garage into living space.
  • Pool house or backyard office. Similar construction, with a scope that ranges from a changing room to a full guest suite.

Which fits your lot?

The answer depends on lot size, setbacks, access, utilities and your city's rules. A stick-built home is framed on site, so it can fit lots where a delivered unit cannot. The fastest way to find out is a free feasibility check followed by a property analysis.
